title: A Cache That Expires
description: Implement TTL expiry and a background janitor on a small cache, then watch the whole test suite verify hours of behaviour in a quarter of a second inside synctest bubbles.
short_description: Write time-dependent code and test it without waiting
learning_objectives: Implement TTL expiry against time.Now rather than a counter
Write a ticker loop that shuts down on context cancellation
Read a test that uses synctest.Test and synctest.Wait
Explain why the bubble makes a timing test deterministic
real_world_connection: Caches, retries, rate limiters and heartbeats all behave correctly only after some delay. Before synctest, testing them meant sleeping and hoping, which is where a large share of flaky CI failures come from.
requirements: Get returns a miss for unknown keys and for entries past their expiry
Get still hits one second before the TTL
Cleanup deletes expired entries on every tick
Cleanup leaves live entries alone and returns when the context is cancelled
bonus_points: Remove the ticker and sleep in a loop instead, then see which test starts failing
Add a test that asserts Cleanup has removed nothing before the first tick
